pubs.name: George
pubs.address: 75 Borough High St, London SE1 1NH, UK

examples:
My wife and I have been to the George a few times during our visits to London (we're from Chicago).

The history is a big draw and deservedly so.  There are multiple bars, restaurants in this establishment, some older than others.

The few meals that we've had there are what I would call traditional pub food.  Additionally, the beer selection is very good with something being served for every palette.

Being close to Borough Market is a plus.  If you need a break or simply looking for something to eat, this is a great spot to pay a visit.

Having been loyal lunchtime customers for over 16 years, we have come to expect a good standard of service and food. Not this time. We decided to sit outside for a change. The tables were so close together it was difficult to get seated. (Crammed in for Wimbledon and the World cup on the big (noisy) screen. We ordered a Camembert and Mushroom Galette. No idea what they brought, but it wasn't what was ordered. We also ordered two medium sirloin steaks. I've never tasted anything like it in my life. First, it was very nearly still mooing, second, it was full of gristle and fat . Inedible. The replacement Camembert and Mushroom arrived and guess what, it was STILL wrong. Eventually, after much discussion, the manager agreed to refund the cost, and supplied a plate of chips, as the other two diners had "finished " eating. We have always had good service and the correct order in the upstairs gallery restaurant from every staff member over the years. It's very sad that a much loved lunch venue will never again receive our custom.

pubs.name: Anchor Bankside
pubs.address: 34 Park St, London SE1 9EF, UK

examples: A beautiful day up London and the best pub to be in. Had a beer in the garden and one on the roof top terrace. I’m normally an ale guy but when the weather is this great a nice cold lager is the one! Cheers, Mike @the_man_cave_est2021

During our many visits to London, we had walked past this pub countless times. The exterior alone is stunning, and its location is absolutely fantastic.

Today, we finally decided to step inside for a nice pint. As beautiful as the pub is on the outside, it is just as impressive on the inside, what an amazing place!

There is a very wide selection of beers, ales, and other craft brews. The atmosphere is warm, relaxed, and incredibly welcoming. It's the perfect spot to sit down, catch up with friends, and enjoy a great beer together. Cheers!

Popped in for a pint after going to Borough Market.   Nice spot on the corner,  food looked lovely but we'd eaten.   Had a nice pint of Level Head,  lovely. Proper old school pub, good atmosphere.  Apparently rebuilt in 1676 after the great fire of London.

This is the place you go for Fish and chips, Scotch eggs or Sunday Roast beef dinner with Yorkshire pudding. Amazing atmosphere, so many little pockets of bars and stairs, it's such a delight to eat there. Super friendly staff.

We had Sunday roast at The Anchor Bankside and overall it was a good experience, mainly thanks to the flavour of the main dishes.

We ordered the 28-day aged sirloin of beef. The taste was very good, but there’s an important downside: if this is sirloin, it was much fattier than expected. The portions came as two relatively small medallions with quite a bit of fat, which made them less enjoyable to eat. The sides were decent, though a bit heavy on fried elements.

We also tried the Nut Roast Wellington, which was actually a pleasant surprise — very tasty and well balanced.

Desserts, however, were disappointing. We had the Chocolate Caramel Torte and the Blackberry & Elderflower Eton Mess, and both felt quite underwhelming compared to the mains.

Recommendation:
Enjoy the Sunday roast, but skip the desserts, or go for the classic Sticky Toffee Pudding, which is likely a safer choice.

Overall: great flavour in the mains, but some details (especially fat content and desserts) could be improved.

pubs.name: The Crosse Keys
pubs.address: 9 Gracechurch St, London EC3V 0DR, UK

examples:
We went for the pre new year eve, and the place was incredible, a truly authentic English pub. We entered through the back entrance, which comes from a dark and secluded path, and it was magical when we found ourselves inside. The atmosphere was pure British joy, as families and friends.
We tasted the fish and chips, which is their signature dish, and it was delicious, along with the Guinness and Carlsberg beers, and it was a great great night.
Thanks Berna and Kari for this wonderful time.

The Crosse Keys on Gracechurch Street is one of the most impressive pubs in the City of London, especially if you enjoy historic interiors and classic British pub atmosphere. Housed inside a former banking hall, the building feels grand and spacious, with high ceilings, marble pillars, ornate décor, and a striking central bar that immediately stands out.

As a JD Wetherspoon pub, it offers very good value for central London, with a wide range of ales, lagers, and affordable food options. The beer selection is especially strong, often featuring several real ales and guest beers. The food is standard pub fare, but reliable, filling, and reasonably priced for the location.

The atmosphere changes depending on the time of day — quieter during mornings and afternoons, then becoming lively and busy with City workers in the evenings. Despite the size of the venue, it still manages to feel welcoming rather than overwhelming.

Service can occasionally slow down during peak hours, but the overall experience is usually positive thanks to the unique setting and good value. If you are near Monument or Leadenhall Market and want a traditional London pub with character, The Crosse Keys is definitely worth visiting.

pubs.name: The Woolpack
pubs.address: 98 Bermondsey St, Bridge, London SE1 3UB, UK

examples: I have never been to The Woolpack before  but my daughter said she'd heard good things about it. Although our daughter lives in London, we (my husband and I) were only up for a visit. We didn't book and just turned up a about 6ish. The ground floor was full and the staff said there were a couple of tables free upstairs. We went up a large circular staircase to the next floor and although it also was full, we managed to get the last remaining table. After ordering drinks, we ordered a shared starter, hummus with a lovely bread, sprinkled with herbs. Delicious! Throughout the visit we were looked after by 2 great servers unfortunately we don't know the name of the Chinese man, but our main server was Joe. Both of them looked after us very well. The main meals arrived, and they were delicious. There wasn't any rush, because they needed the tables. We were felt very relaxed. We had a lovely evening, the atmosphere was great,  not too loud. The service and the food were very good.  We would definitely visit again.  Thank you.

Went to the Woolpack in Bermondsey Street, London today for a roast.
We loved the seating in our own box, and that our dog was able to join us.
However, it was not clear how you would order food, as no one seemed to come to the table.  So we ended up going to the bar to order everything.
We ordered roast and they came out 10 minutes later.  This was really fast and the food needed to be hotter as it was luke warm.  The food was good.
When we came to ordering dessert they seemed to have ran out even though it was so early on in the day.  Therefore, we suspected that the numbers were not properly looked at for potential food orders.  We were going to nothing and go elsewhere, when they said they had sticky toffee pudding which was nit on the menu.  On the online menu it said it was £6, but it was over £8 which surprised us.
Something that is really important to me is accessibility due to my disabilities.  One of the main reasons for my 3 star review is because of the things above and the quite obvious lack of support of facilities for me.
Be prepared that there is not a lot of room to negotiate around the place.  The men’s toilets were very unfriendly, tight, and inappropriate for someone like me.  There is no accessible toilet, which would have made the trip here a lot better and less awkward.
I was shocked at the price of lemonade and blackcurrant, as a non-alcoholic drinker, it was nearly as much as my friend’s pint. 🍺
I feel the pub could make changes to accommodate people with disabilities.
Also, the menu is very much geared toward vegans and vegetarians.

pubs.address: London EC3N 4AA, UK

examples: Excellent experience! Tasty and value for money pub in the heart of London. We ordered 3 burguers  with the drinks deal, so we got also 3 drinks and we paid 9,40 £ for each dish, the food and drinks were good. The place is amazing. We ate our food close to a window with a nice view of the tower Bridge. One of the best places that we could find in London with good prices and food. The only flaw was the service. Our table was dirty and we asked them for a cloth or something to clean it, but the told us that they will come to clean it, but that never happened. They were no nice at order time. But everything else was amazing! A definitely recommended experience if you are looking for a worth place in London.

I recently enjoyed a fantastic English breakfast at Wetherspoon, and I cannot recommend it highly enough! The breakfast was truly delicious, featuring all the classic elements cooked to perfection. What surprised me the most was the price – it was incredibly reasonable for London, making it a great value for such a hearty meal.

Additionally, the interior of the venue was lovely, creating a warm and inviting atmosphere that made my dining experience even better. If you're looking for a satisfying breakfast without breaking the bank, Wetherspoon is definitely the place to go. Highly recommended!

Possibly the nicest Spoons we've visited The food is great and better value in this location than other establishments. Drinks are nearly half price in comparison too.
Great location with view of Tower Bridge and The Tower of London .
It was quite busy, but we found a table on the upper floor. Great decoration and atmosphere. We tried the Spice Bag which had quite a kick. Ordered from the app, just a 10 minute wait. Definitely worth a visit.

Came here for a cheeky spoons breakfast, we managed to get seated easily even on a Saturday and we ordered on the app. We were served very quickly and Osman brought our refillable mugs within a couple of minutes. The food was what you would expect from a wetherspoons,  cheap and cheerful but for under £8 it was great. Won't get better value for money in London. Our server was excellent.  Osman went out of his way to not only check on us and make sure we knew where everything was, but also engaged with kids that seemed unsettled.  He was very friendly and polite and deserves a pay rise (tried my best Osman). Would highly recommend.

pubs.name: The Counting House, EC3
pubs.address: 50 Cornhill, London EC3V 3PD, UK

examples: We visited the Couting House for a drink while doing the usual tourist thing in the City of London. The staff were friendly and the drinks prices no worse than any other London pub. The interior was magnificent with a large island bar, polished wooden staircase, mosaic tile floor, very high ceiling with chandeliers and a glass dome roof as well as a mezanine balcony, upstairs dining and several side rooms as well as a terrace at the rear for smokers. There were lots of historical pictures and adornments to look at. Well worth a visit if you're in the area.

We weren't aware this was a hotel as well as a pub but we went in on the of chance we could get breakfast here... which they can do and it's available to non residents. We had the full English breakfast and the avocado on toast. The full English had high quality items and was delicious.  The avocado was also very tasty with an addition of a pesto dressing which was well received too.

Great location on an old historic bank and helpful friendly staff.  Highly recommended for breakfast!

We stayed at The Counting House from 24 to 28 April (4 nights) and had the Angel room. It’s a lovely, spacious and very tidy room with a comfortable double bed. The bathroom was also large and well laid out, with a shower, sink and toilet. A small detail, but appreciated: plenty of hooks for towels and jackets.

The room had a fridge and a safe, and the air conditioning worked perfectly. We had no problem storing our clothes and suitcases — there was plenty of space.

From the moment we arrived, the staff were genuinely friendly and explained everything clearly. Housekeeping was excellent: the bed was made neatly every day and towels were replaced when we wanted them changed.

Breakfast is served in the pub on the ground floor. Again, a warm welcome and a really nice, generous breakfast in a great setting. The pub is also a great place for a drink and dinner — we ate there twice and enjoyed it both times.

The location is a big plus: right in the Bank district (London City), close to St Paul’s Cathedral and very near the Underground. At night it was wonderfully quiet — we didn’t hear a thing and slept very well.

All in all, this hotel is absolutely worth recommending, and we’d happily stay here again.

pubs.address: 2, 4 Tooley St, London SE1 2SY, UK

examples:
Great spot for watching live football games! The atmosphere is electric during matches, with big screens, loud crowd energy, and that classic bierkeller vibe with long shared tables.

Perfect place to go with friends – good selection of beers, quick service even when it’s busy, and a really social, lively setting. You really feel the game here.

If you’re looking for a place in London to enjoy football with a proper match-day atmosphere, this is definitely a top choice!

OMG. THIS IS IT! I've lived in London for over 30 years and we've just found the best pub in London. I asked and it's been here since lockdown. We also have been doing Airbnb for 16 years and also send people to Waxy O'Connor. (Still good). But the Bermonsey Bierkeller has it all. Good food, entertainment, very friendly and helpful service. It feels very personal and, wait for it, several toilets for both that are clean (and spacious!)!! The games? I might miss a few, but it has an awesome minigolf (9 holes), karting, pool, darts,  shuffleboard, axe throwing and more. Oh, and I hear it will have a karaoke room soon. Oh, and it's perfect for watching footy. Plenty screens in the dining area. If I could give this 6 stars, I definitely would.
Tried the mini golf and it was a fun experience - spooky themed! Nani the host and bartender was very friendly and provided a great service. Will definitely return to try the other activities

pubs.name: The Roebuck
pubs.address: 50 Great Dover St, London SE1 4YG, UK

examples:
Food was really good and reasonably priced. There’s a solid menu with plenty of choice and includes some considered vegetarian options, which is always a plus.

Drinks wise there’s a strong selection of beers with a nice mix of local and speciality options, so it doesn’t feel like a generic pub offering.

Despite it being peak hours, the staff were friendly, calm and attentive throughout the evening.

The building itself is beautiful. A Grade II listed pub with loads of characters, high ceilings, lots of natural light.

Good atmosphere, lively, but not so loud that you can actually have a proper conversation without shouting at each other.

Great pub!

🚇 Borough
🍺 £6.90 Pillars Pilsner

The Roebuck is located halfway down Great Dover Street in Borough, South London. The nearest Tube is Borough.

Close by on Tabard Street and Hankey Place are Stretcher Railings. These are fences which are recycled World War II stretchers. They are worth a look as part of a visit to the pub.

The Roebuck was built in 1892 and is Grade II listed ex-Truman’s pub. This handsome Victorian building has mansard roofing, Dutch gables and a green dome-like roof structure, making it one of London’s most attractive pubs.

This is good size one bar pub that has a contemporary feel with nice traditional touches. At the heart of this pub is an Island servery with elegant corinthian columns and lots of foliage above the back bar. The main bar area forms a horseshoe shape around the servery and is bathed in light from the beautiful arched windows. To the rear of the servery is a snug complete with a fireplace and comfy sofas. The overall decor comprises of a boarding floor, pastel coloured walls, rustic tables and chairs and a mixture of colourful prints and mirrors. Upstairs is a function room where Charlie Chaplin supposedly performed.

The beer selection is on point and offers a selection of four cask ales and keg options from local London breweries. I decided on a Pillars Pilsner, my pint was excellent, price point was a little high. The food option is classic pub fayre, a large portion of Fish & Chips costs £17, Roasts are available on a Sunday.

I arrived around 12.30pm on a mild Saturday lunchtime in February. The pub was initially calm and relaxed but soon filled up with hordes of punters, in to watch the Six Nations rugby. The atmosphere was upbeat with an expectant buzz around the pub. The service was friendly and personable, the team on duty were enthusiastic and ready for a busy day’s trade.

Jaw dropping architecture, comfortable surroundings, a good selection of beer and friendly service, made for a marvellous pub experience, put this one on the must visit list.

pubs.name: The Barrowboy & Banker, SE1
pubs.address: 6-8 Borough High St, London SE1 9QQ, UK

examples:
A classic London pub with a grand, slightly upscale feel, set inside a converted old bank near London Bridge. The interior is a standout — high ceilings, big windows, and a dramatic staircase give it a more impressive vibe than your average pub.

Food is solid British pub fare — especially known for pies, fish & chips, and a good range of ales. Portions are generous and it’s a reliable choice if you want something traditional.

pubs.name: The Rose & Crown, London Bridge (PUBLOVE)
pubs.address: 65 Union St, London SE1 1SG, UK

examples:
You get what you pay for.
The rooms are rather cramped and small.
You have three bunk beds with very little head space, so watch out for that.
The space to store your valuables is limited, so decide what you want to put in there.
The bathrooms are inlaid, so they might get humid when you shower in there. They were absolute clean though.
The staff is super friendly and is always happy to assist with your problems.
They take your issues seriously and react accordingly and super fast!
The food and drinks are very good, the atmosphere nice.
It's a popular pub and always buzzing with locals in the evening. You don't hear any of that in the hostel though.
We had the breakfast and that was very nice and filling.
The location of the hostel convenient. You have the Borough market close by which has amazing food.
And a place called "Where the pancakes are" just around the corner. Best pancakes I had in my entire life.

I haven’t stayed in the hostel, however I’ve visited the pub. We were there at the lunch time and we got special deal menu ; fries plus cheeseburger. I wasn’t expecting too much since it was a random pub visit but I have tasted the best fries ever. The cheeseburger was awesome too. Bartenders were super kind and they even let me taste the beers since I didn’t know the tastes. Definetly visit again and recommend!!!

Staff - very very friendly and helpful. 24 hour service so you feel safe and not restricted.

I would stay again to be honest - can't beat the price and location!

It's clear it's a pub run by nice people who care. We'll be back, for sure

pubs.address: Bridge Station, London SE1 9SP, UK

examples: Place was very nice , Our waiter Jordan was polite and explained everything about drinks and food, our recommendations for stopping by and trying a delicious burger.

I can imagine this place to be heaving on the weekend or when there is a game on. However we visited midweek and it was fairly quiet.

We were slightly wary because of it being a sports bar but we took the plunge and dropped in for dinner.

Blimey, the staff are good. So on the ball and very friendly. Mark was a particular stand out. He made sure our glasses were never empty and kept an eye on the table throughout the visit.

We opted for the sharing plates and that was a good shout. The lamb kofta and mac ‘n’ cheese bite were the stars of the show.  We had 5 dishes in total and that is just about enough for two people.

Overall a very good visit. We will be back!

pubs.name: Bermondsey Bar & Kitchen
pubs.address: 40 Bermondsey St, London SE1 3UD, UK

examples:
We booked an outdoor table for a group of 15 here, and it was a success. Check-in to our tables was quick and easy and our tables were very clean and with plenty of space.

Drinks and food are ordered through a QR code and they arrive very quickly, which had a very positive impact on our experience. We would receive drinks within a few minutes of ordering, whereas queueing up for a drink at Vinegar Yard next door could take 20 - 25 minutes on the same day.

Door staff and floor staff were pleasant, there were no crazy queues for toilets, and the food was decent.

Would happily return here with friends if we were in search of a great beer garden near London Bridge.

A special shoutout to Dhrumil, whose service truly stood out. There was a small delay with our order, but he handled it exceptionally well - kept us updated, and made sure everything was taken care of without us even having to ask. That level of attentiveness really made a difference.

Will definitely be visiting again!

Great spot in Bermondsey. The food is fresh, the drinks are solid, and the vibe is just right relaxed but lively. The outdoor space is perfect for sunny afternoons, and the staff are always welcoming. One of those places you end up staying longer than you planned.

The Bermondsey Bar and Kitchen located just to the south of London Bridge Station is a fine venue with a good offering of keg beers to keep their menu company. Lovely staff and good service. Fun to visit.

Ben, the manager, really deserves recognition - he was extremely polite, attentive, and kept a cool head even when there were issues with the printer and tills.

The venue itself is decent, if a little tired, but it’s in a great location, which makes it especially busy on peak nights. That said, it feels like senior management or the owner should review staffing levels during those key shifts, as the team seemed quite overwhelmed.

Given how hard the staff were working under pressure, anything less than 5 stars wouldn’t feel fair. Well done guys! 👏🏻

pubs.name: Bunch of Grapes
pubs.address: 2 St Thomas St, London SE1 9RS, UK

examples:
Visited on a Monday at 5pm, so maybe  different experience to a Thursday or weekend night, but...
Thoroughly enjoyable pub on a quiet night.
Good choice of lagers, alcohol and zero, plus some good whiskeys.
Staff were friendly and helpful. Tables were cleared promptly and we almost never had to wait to be served.
Had a great table in the rear courtyard which has some tables in shade and some in sun, and a retractable canopy over some of them too. Smoking is allowed outside in this area, and although it didn't bother us at all, and few smokers there anyway, it's something to be aware of if you hate smoke.
Food was good. A nice burger and fries, not greaay and bacon while not overly crispy didn't suffer despite that. Only reason it was 4 not 5 stars is because it's pricey at £18!
Overall, a good venue in a great location of getting home from London Bridge! Would recommend.

Wanted to have a traditional pub experience. Came to Bunch of Grapes and had a great time. Mark was a great server and the food was great. There were rugby matches happening, so the environment was lively

We decided to have a spot of lunch here, while returning to London Bridge.
The pub is small and quaint but the team are really friendly.
Downstairs was busy, so we sat upstairs.
On entering we were greeted by our server Rhys, who was very friendly and attentive. He seated us and gave us a few minutes to decide what we wanted to eat before we ordered.
Our food came out quickly, we ordered 1 vegan Wellington roast, 1 fish and chips and a beef rib burger.
The food was exceptional (they even checked if i was vegan or vegetarian, so i could have a yorkshire pudding!! No-one has ever done that before!). Our chef was called Ben and he had done himself proud with the meals.. the Vegan Wellington was better than i could imagine, and the roasties, well i could have just eaten a plateful of those!!
We come to London Bridge regularly, but i am ashamed to say i didn't even know The Bunch of Grapes was there! But know i know we will be back!!
Thank you for a great experience Bunch of Grapes!

We decided to have a spot of lunch here, while returning to London Bridge.
The pub is small and quaint but the team are really friendly.
Downstairs was busy, so we sat upstairs.
On entering we were greeted by our server Rhys, who was very friendly and attentive. He seated us and gave us a few minutes to decide what we wanted to eat before we ordered.
Our food came out quickly, we ordered 1 vegan Wellington roast, 1 fish and chips and a beef rib burger.
The food was exceptional (they even checked if i was vegan or vegetarian, so i could have a yorkshire pudding!! No-one has ever done that before!). Our chef was called Ben and he had done himself proud with the meals.. the Vegan Wellington was better than i could imagine, and the roasties, well i could have just eaten a plateful of those!!
We come to London Bridge regularly, but i am ashamed to say i didn't even know The Bunch of Grapes was there! But know i know we will be back!!
Thank you for a great experience Bunch of Grapes!

pubs.name: Polite Vicar
pubs.address: 600 Etruria Rd, Basford, Newcastle-under-Lyme, Newcastle ST5 0LU, UK

examples:
We’ve visited a couple of times now and generally have a good experience. The food quality is good overall, and the atmosphere is excellent. The ribs are particularly nice, while the steak is decent but not the highest quality I’ve had.

The staff are a bit mixed. Some are very friendly and helpful, while others aren’t quite as welcoming. On one visit, we were accidentally given an alcoholic drink after specifically requesting a non alcoholic option as I was driving home. The restaurant wasn’t particularly busy at the time, so that was a disappointing mistake.

For a Greene King, the prices are reasonable and it’s definitely one of the better ones in the Stoke area. The desserts are also very good, especially the chocolate fudge cake. The only issue is consistency – sometimes it arrives warm, which is perfect, while other times it comes out cold. I’d also personally like to see a little more ice cream served with it, although that’s just a personal preference.

Overall, it’s a good place to eat with a great atmosphere, tasty food, and fair prices. A few improvements in service consistency and attention to detail would make it even better.

The PV is my favourite pub to visit! All the staff are so friendly and they all work incredibly hard! Food is always really nice and affordable with loads of deals on. Atmosphere is always pleasant even when there are things on like big football matches, it’s still family friendly! Highly recommend to everyone!

Had our tea here on a Saturday evening it seems to get very busy at weekends as people were getting turned away who hadn't previously booked.
The service & food on our visit was very good, the menu is large & we ordered beef lasagne ( with a side salad) , garlic bread with cheese for my partner whilst I had 3 small plates ( tapas style) crispy prawns, beef tacos & portion of nachos all tasty & presented well bill came to under £ 23.00 this is a 'sizzling pub' and we have one locally on merseyside   but wasn't too happy with the food there on our last visit ( 18 months ago) so it does seem it can vary from pub to pub, happy to report everything was  great at the polite vicar 😋
Went on Sunday lunch, food was nice it wasn't too busy. We were told the waiting time was an hour but food came out quicker. Staff were friendly.

pubs.name: Cotton Mill
pubs.address: Liverpool Rd, Newcastle-under-Lyme, Newcastle ST5 2AF, UK

examples:
We visited The Cotton Mill recently and overall had a decent evening, though there were a few things worth noting.
One surprise was that there was a quiz night happening. We do sometimes enjoy quizzes, but we weren’t expecting the loud PA announcements during dinner which made the atmosphere a bit more like a pub event than a relaxed meal.
We had one of the 40% off mains coupons from a mailer, and honestly this made a big difference to how we felt about the value. At full price it probably wouldn’t have felt worth it, but with the discount it was reasonable.
The ribs looked great (see photo) and there was also a triple burger special listed at £18.99 before the discount. The burgers were okay, but the beef was clearly overcooked and the portion was smaller than the picture on the specials menu suggested.
I also ordered wings as a starter (£6.50) and unfortunately they were a bit laughable — very small and not great value.
Another issue was timing of the food. They brought out the starter and then everyone else had to wait quite a while for their mains. It would have made much more sense to bring everything together.
Drinks pricing was probably the biggest shock. A Pepsi was £4.65 and a pint of Guinness was over £6. At those prices it feels pretty steep — especially for soft drinks. If cola is going to cost that much, it would be nice if refills were offered.
That said, the staff were genuinely very nice. Our server (a young black girl whose name I unfortunately didn’t catch) was friendly and pleasant throughout. The gentleman who seemed to be the manager was also very polite and attentive, and the bar staff were nice as well.
Overall we did enjoy the evening, and with the discount the meal felt acceptable value, but there are definitely some areas where things could be improved.

pubs.name: The Victoria
pubs.address: 62 King St, Newcastle-under-Lyme, Newcastle ST5 1HX, UK

examples:
The Victors (Little Vic) is a fantastic pub with a warm, welcoming atmosphere that makes everyone feel at home. There’s a great selection of drinks to suit all tastes, whether you fancy a pint, a glass of wine, or something a little different.

One of the things that makes The Little Vic stand out is the variety of events they host. From enjoyable Cheese & Wine evenings and lively pub quizzes to fun-filled karaoke nights and much more, there’s always something happening to bring the community together.

The staff are all incredibly friendly, creating a relaxed and enjoyable environment for everyone. A special mention goes to Sophie, the lovely landlady, who works hard to make every visit memorable and ensures all guests receive a warm welcome.

If you’re looking for a great local pub with a friendly atmosphere, excellent drinks, and brilliant entertainment, The Little Vic is definitely worth a visit.

One of the things that makes The Little Vic stand out is the variety of events they host. From enjoyable Cheese & Wine evenings and lively pub quizzes to fun-filled karaoke nights and much more, there’s always something happening to bring the community together.

The staff are all incredibly friendly, creating a relaxed and enjoyable environment for everyone. A special mention goes to Sophie, the lovely landlady, who works hard to make every visit memorable and ensures all guests receive a warm welcome.

If you’re looking for a great local pub with a friendly atmosphere, excellent drinks, and brilliant entertainment, The Little Vic is definitely worth a visit.

examples: Really good curry menu, authentic homemade food. Hospitality was 10/10. Food was exceptional, I do a lot of curries and this was probably the best so far. Worth a visit to the area just to go to Noahs. Selection of British food on the menu too which looked good on other people's plates.

Wow! What a meal we have just had here.

From the chutney which was the best we have ever had, my fiancé had two bowls of their house made chutney. To the amazing mixed grill platter for two.

The food was outstanding. We then got to the mains and it just got better and better.

The staff are great and we recommend this as a must try restaurant.

I was really looking forward to visiting this pub, but unfortunately my experience was ruined before I even stepped inside. I was refused entry simply because I was wearing an England shirt, and to make matters worse, they weren’t showing the national football match.

It’s incredibly disappointing that a place that should be about community and good times would turn away customers over something as harmless as supporting their national team. Football is part of our culture, and wearing a shirt shouldn’t be a reason to exclude anyone.

I left feeling unwelcome and won’t be returning. If you’re a football fan hoping for a friendly atmosphere, I’d recommend looking elsewhere.

pubs.name: The Greyhound
pubs.address: 67 George St, Newcastle-under-Lyme, Stoke-on-Trent, Newcastle ST5 1JT, UK

examples:
Walking up to Artisan Tap for one of the three sold out The Bluetones concerts taking place, I noticed a pub near the main road crossing. The outside has two entrances to the pub and a number of benches. The pub is separated into three rooms, with bars in two of them.

Although hot food/ chip butties are only served on Sunday during Quiz Night, the venue has a very good selection of sausage rolls and crisps. The back of the bar features spirits, wines, bottles of cider, soft drinks and Titanic's own gin. The front of the bars feature a mix of Real Ale Cask and Keg of macro beers, guests beers and a wonderful range of Titanic's own beers.

From my first visit, Chloe, Ellie and all the other staff have been absolutely wonderful. When I walked in on this visit, Chloe gave me a great welcome (with Chloe being very kind and friendly to regulars, and those visiting the pub for the first time.) Learning that Titanic has released a limited edition beer, I went for half of the delightful Iceberg Grand Crew on Cask. Whilst having the drink, I looked at the cleverly laid out Titanic newspaper clippings across the walls. Saying thank you to Chloe for the drink, I sailed off to a concert.

examples:
We’ve visited a couple of times now and generally have a good experience. The food quality is good overall, and the atmosphere is excellent. The ribs are particularly nice, while the steak is decent but not the highest quality I’ve had.

The staff are a bit mixed. Some are very friendly and helpful, while others aren’t quite as welcoming. On one visit, we were accidentally given an alcoholic drink after specifically requesting a non alcoholic option as I was driving home. The restaurant wasn’t particularly busy at the time, so that was a disappointing mistake.

For a Greene King, the prices are reasonable and it’s definitely one of the better ones in the Stoke area. The desserts are also very good, especially the chocolate fudge cake. The only issue is consistency – sometimes it arrives warm, which is perfect, while other times it comes out cold. I’d also personally like to see a little more ice cream served with it, although that’s just a personal preference.

Overall, it’s a good place to eat with a great atmosphere, tasty food, and fair prices. A few improvements in service consistency and attention to detail would make it even better.

The service & food on our visit was very good, the menu is large & we ordered beef lasagne ( with a side salad) , garlic bread with cheese for my partner whilst I had 3 small plates ( tapas style) crispy prawns, beef tacos & portion of nachos all tasty & presented well bill came to under £ 23.00 this is a 'sizzling pub' and we have one locally on merseyside   but wasn't too happy with the food there on our last visit ( 18 months ago) so it does seem it can vary from pub to pub, happy to report everything was  great at the polite vicar 😋

Stopped on the off chance whilst out and fancied a Sunday roast, we did not have a reservation so unsure if we could be accommodated. Staff were really friendly and looked at openings for us. It turned out that one reservation had not turned up so we were offered that table. We had 3 traditional turkey roasts (turkey tasted smoked which was unusual) (not sure if it was supposed to be) but was very nice regardless. Lovely family atmosphere and appeared to be dog friendly. very reasonably priced and thoroughly enjoyed the visit. Will be going back. Thank you.

We’ve visited a couple of times now and generally have a good experience. The food quality is good overall, and the atmosphere is excellent. The ribs are particularly nice, while the steak is decent but not the highest quality I’ve had.

The staff are a bit mixed. Some are very friendly and helpful, while others aren’t quite as welcoming. On one visit, we were accidentally given an alcoholic drink after specifically requesting a non alcoholic option as I was driving home. The restaurant wasn’t particularly busy at the time, so that was a disappointing mistake.

For a Greene King, the prices are reasonable and it’s definitely one of the better ones in the Stoke area. The desserts are also very good, especially the chocolate fudge cake. The only issue is consistency – sometimes it arrives warm, which is perfect, while other times it comes out cold. I’d also personally like to see a little more ice cream served with it, although that’s just a personal preference.

Overall, it’s a good place to eat with a great atmosphere, tasty food, and fair prices. A few improvements in service consistency and attention to detail would make it even better.

pubs.name: The Rigger
pubs.address: Marsh Parade, Newcastle-under-Lyme, Newcastle ST5 1BT, UK

examples:
An excellent little live music venue!
Great stage, dance floor & sound set-up.
Staff were all really helpful, too (thanks to the barmaid for the local food recommendations!)
I wish it wasn't so far away from me 😂 but I'm sure I'll make the trip again in the future, now I know how good it is.

First time at this live music venue & apart from the REALLY uncomfortable fold up chairs we had an enjoyable night watching Tom Robinson.
Staff are friendly & bar prices are reasonable i would definitely return but choose to stand next time 😃

I wish it wasn't so far away from me 😂 but I'm sure I'll make the trip again in the future, now I know how good it is.

First time visit to see punk band 999, with support from the excellent Wasted Life, and the also excellent Kid Klumsy.
Cracking little venue with good friendly staff at all levels, if you know Rock City Nottingham,I would say it's around the same size as the downstairs area, with an area at the rear where you can play pool and have a breather as it gets really hot down the front. Sound quality was excellent for a venue of this size. Bar prices seemed average although we didn't notice any special offers as neither of us drink nowadays. Will most certainly be coming here again. Oh, and it was really easy to find.

Staff are friendly & bar prices are reasonable i would definitely return but choose to stand next time 😃

A cosy place with a long bar pool table at one end & a smallish stage & viewiing area. I went to see Theatre of Hate with the greeat Kirk Brandon on Vocals & lead guitar. I was pleasantly surprised to see Stan Stammers on base as I had heard that he had been ill & may not attend. They were fantastic as always celebrating the anniversary of the Westworld album playing every track. I sang every word to every tune out loud & loved every minute. Standouts were Original Sin, Conquistador, Legion, Westworld & Incinerator. Everything I touch and hold it then turns into Stone ! Stone !

pubs.name: Victoria Hotel
pubs.address: Brampton Rd, May Bank, Newcastle-under-Lyme, Newcastle ST5 0SJ, UK

examples:
This has genuinely shocked me. It was my first time visiting the Victoria Hotel, and I have to say the food was extremely disappointing.

I think the chef needs to revisit basic cooking temperatures and grill standards. We ordered two medium-rare steaks, a combo sharer, a mixed grill, a kids' roast, a chicken schnitzel, and a Caesar salad.

The two medium-rare steaks arrived burnt, so we sent them back. Unfortunately, when they came back out, they were even worse and had been cooked well done.

I also ordered the mixed grill, which really set the standard for the rest of the meal. The sausages were burnt, the steak was burnt, the chicken was dry, and the gammon was dry. Somehow, even the peas were dry and didn't taste fresh. The only parts of the meal that were acceptable were the items that had simply been fried or served with gravy.

The food arrived reasonably quickly, in around 30 minutes, but the quality was far below what I expected. The only saving grace was that the staff refunded two of the meals.

I've always believed that if a kitchen can't cook a decent mixed grill, it's difficult to have confidence in the rest of the menu. Sadly, this experience has put me off returning for food. If I do come back, it will probably only be for something simple like a burger or other fried food.

The service was great, and the staff were polite and helpful throughout, but unfortunately the food was very poor.

A huge thank you to the wonderful staff at the Victoria! Our book club met up there last night for our monthly meeting and it was wonderful. Plenty of space for us all, lots of food and drink options, and the staff couldn’t do enough for us. Great evening!!!

Lovely traditional pub food, although if you're having the steak, request it be cooked one less than you want (my medium-rare was medium and my dad's medium was medium-well). Overall our party of 6 all enjoyed what they ordered.

Service was a little on the slow side. For context, we arrived at 5pm, ordered at 5:25pm, starters (2) came out at 5:55pm, mains (6) at 6:20pm.

Due to the hot weather, it is very warm inside. That's no fault of the establishment, but might be useful information for visitors thinking of going during the hot weather.

Overall it'd say this is a 3.5 out of 5. Good for the price.

pubs.name: Cotton Mill
pubs.address: Liverpool Rd, Newcastle-under-Lyme, Newcastle ST5 2AF, UK

examples:
We visited The Cotton Mill recently and overall had a decent evening, though there were a few things worth noting.
One surprise was that there was a quiz night happening. We do sometimes enjoy quizzes, but we weren’t expecting the loud PA announcements during dinner which made the atmosphere a bit more like a pub event than a relaxed meal.
We had one of the 40% off mains coupons from a mailer, and honestly this made a big difference to how we felt about the value. At full price it probably wouldn’t have felt worth it, but with the discount it was reasonable.
The ribs looked great (see photo) and there was also a triple burger special listed at £18.99 before the discount. The burgers were okay, but the beef was clearly overcooked and the portion was smaller than the picture on the specials menu suggested.
I also ordered wings as a starter (£6.50) and unfortunately they were a bit laughable — very small and not great value.
Another issue was timing of the food. They brought out the starter and then everyone else had to wait quite a while for their mains. It would have made much more sense to bring everything together.
Drinks pricing was probably the biggest shock. A Pepsi was £4.65 and a pint of Guinness was over £6. At those prices it feels pretty steep — especially for soft drinks. If cola is going to cost that much, it would be nice if refills were offered.
That said, the staff were genuinely very nice. Our server (a young black girl whose name I unfortunately didn’t catch) was friendly and pleasant throughout. The gentleman who seemed to be the manager was also very polite and attentive, and the bar staff were nice as well.
Overall we did enjoy the evening, and with the discount the meal felt acceptable value, but there are definitely some areas where things could be improved.

Came here for Valentine’s Day
Service was amazing , quick and the staff were all so friendly and welcoming.
Food was hot and came out fast.
Nice sized portions and well presented
Will be returning again soon

Overall we did enjoy the evening, and with the discount the meal felt acceptable value, but there are definitely some areas where things could be improved.

pubs.address: 62 King St, Newcastle-under-Lyme, Newcastle ST5 1HX, UK

examples:
The Victors (Little Vic) is a fantastic pub with a warm, welcoming atmosphere that makes everyone feel at home. There’s a great selection of drinks to suit all tastes, whether you fancy a pint, a glass of wine, or something a little different.

One of the things that makes The Little Vic stand out is the variety of events they host. From enjoyable Cheese & Wine evenings and lively pub quizzes to fun-filled karaoke nights and much more, there’s always something happening to bring the community together.

The staff are all incredibly friendly, creating a relaxed and enjoyable environment for everyone. A special mention goes to Sophie, the lovely landlady, who works hard to make every visit memorable and ensures all guests receive a warm welcome.

If you’re looking for a great local pub with a friendly atmosphere, excellent drinks, and brilliant entertainment, The Little Vic is definitely worth a visit.

Great cheese and wine night!! And at £10 per person, an absolute bargain. I think we had about 7 wines and plenty of cheese and crackers. We love this pub. How friendly it is and how much they try to offer different experiences 🙌🏼🫶🏻👍🏼

I have stayed at the Vic many times over the past 2 years. It’s such a friendly pub and Sophie and Julie are amazing and look after me so well. It’s been tough being far from home but they’ve made every stay so lovely and they’re so welcoming and accommodating. I’ve stayed in probably all the rooms over this period and each one is so comfy, warm and well equipped. The beds are amazingly comfortable. Everything always works perfectly and all the lovely little touches are very welcomed. It’s also cost friendly and the pub always has a great atmosphere with friendly locals and lots of fun pub quizzes and music going on

Really clean room and lovely staff. Would stay here again.

pubs.name: Yates - Newcastle Under Lyme
pubs.address: 14-16 Ironmarket, Newcastle-under-Lyme, Newcastle ST5 1RF, UK

examples: Came here with a friend for Bottomless Brunch on 2nd May 2026. It was the first time we've had Bottomless Brunch here and we were very impressed! The food choices were good and the drinks menu was extensive with some lovely cocktails to choose from as well as spirits and G&Ts. I arrived before my friend and was greeted very warmly by a lovely member of bar staff (sorry I didn't get their name!) who showed me to our table and offered me a glass of water whilst I waited for my friend to arrive (it was quite a warm day so this was greatly appreciated!). Then we were served by Gabby who was lovely and friendly and very attentive! The drinks kept arriving and we certainly had our money's worth! The cocktails were delicious and freshly made and I can highly recommend the Pornstar Martini! It was a very relaxing time and although the Bottomless Brunch service lasts for 2 hours, we were able sit and finish our remaining drinks with no pressure to leave. The staff are a credit to the company and we enjoyed the whole experience so much that we'll be back soon!

Came for bottomless brunch for a girls afternoon. Food was what you would expect, was nice and cooked well but lets face it, you book bottomless brunch for the drinks not the food. Service however was excellent! Gabby was attentive, bubbly and extremely friendly. Service was impeccable, we did not have to wait long for drinks and she checked on us throughout. Thank you Gabby xx

examples:
Walking up to Artisan Tap for one of the three sold out The Bluetones concerts taking place, I noticed a pub near the main road crossing. The outside has two entrances to the pub and a number of benches. The pub is separated into three rooms, with bars in two of them.

Although hot food/ chip butties are only served on Sunday during Quiz Night, the venue has a very good selection of sausage rolls and crisps. The back of the bar features spirits, wines, bottles of cider, soft drinks and Titanic's own gin. The front of the bars feature a mix of Real Ale Cask and Keg of macro beers, guests beers and a wonderful range of Titanic's own beers.

From my first visit, Chloe, Ellie and all the other staff have been absolutely wonderful. When I walked in on this visit, Chloe gave me a great welcome (with Chloe being very kind and friendly to regulars, and those visiting the pub for the first time.) Learning that Titanic has released a limited edition beer, I went for half of the delightful Iceberg Grand Crew on Cask. Whilst having the drink, I looked at the cleverly laid out Titanic newspaper clippings across the walls. Saying thank you to Chloe for the drink, I sailed off to a concert.
